memory_candidates.content: When an embedded `python3 - <<'PYEOF' ... PYEOF` heredoc is used to run an inline Python script from a bash script, stdin is already consumed by the heredoc supplying the script source itself -- a subsequent `sys.stdin.read()` inside that script returns empty, not the data you intended to pipe in. Fix: write the data to a temp file first and pass its path as an argv element, never try to layer a second stdin stream underneath the heredoc.

A CLI tool that regenerates and commits an artifact into a git repo (e.g. an immutability-pinning snapshot tool) must use `git commit --allow-empty` for the write, not a plain `git commit`. A regeneration whose content happens to be byte-identical to what is already committed (e.g. a --force re-run against an unchanged source) stages nothing via `git add`, so a plain `git commit` fails with exit 1 and no new SHA -- silently breaking any caller expecting every regeneration event to produce a fresh, distinguishable commit.

A naive identifier regex like `[A-Za-z_][A-Za-zA-Z0-9_']*` silently truncates at the first `.`, so it cannot capture Lean's common namespaced/dotted theorem names (e.g. `Proposition.map_injective`) as a single token -- it matches only the leading namespace segment. Any tool parsing real-world Lean declaration names by name should either widen the character class to include `.` or explicitly document (and test for) the dotted-name gap as a known limitation, since Mathlib-style codebases use dotted names pervasively.
